verdict.rationale: Undermind is built for scholarly literature search. It searches the global literature, follows citations and key authors, filters by author, journal and year, resolves DOIs, and reads full-text PDFs. Hands-on users confirm it surfaced papers they had missed in Google Scholar, arXiv, ScienceDirect and PubMed. missing for 10: documentation of which corpora and databases are indexed, and coverage of gray literature and theses (users reported it missed much gray literature and few dissertations appeared).

support.subject: As a researcher, I can search scholarly literature and primary sources, not just the open web

citations.quote: Searches the global literature, papers already in the workspace, or a paper’s references and citations in seconds. Filters by author, journal, year, and PDF availability.
Runs a deep literature review from an open-ended research goal and produces a ranked list of papers with a written synthesis.
Reads full-text PDFs in parallel and answers specific questions across many papers at once, including from figures, tables, and equations.
Pretty good: it found some useful references the user had missed in Google Scholar and arXiv.
